venue.name: Naa'Waya'Sum Gardens
venue.description: Naa'Waya'Sum Coastal Indigenous Gardens, formerly the Tofino Botanical Gardens, is a 12 acre site of coastal temperate rainforest with trails, viewpoints and carvings on the Pacific Rim Highway in Tofino. It is part of the Clayoquot Campus, managed by the IISAAK OLAM Foundation and owned by the Clayoquot Indigenous Conservation Innovation Centre, and the grounds are being re-wilded from their former European style botanical garden layout. Entry is by a $10 day pass or an $80 annual membership, and Nuu-chah-nulth citizens and children aged 0 to 12 are free. A cafe and a carving studio and gallery share the same site.
venue.address: 1084 Pacific Rim Hwy, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0

facility_notes.bus_parking: The lodge parking lot can accommodate a maximum of 10 cars.

venue.hours_notes: The gardens page says open 7 days a week, 9:00am to 5:00pm. The carving gallery on the same site is listed separately as Thursday to Sunday 12 to 5pm, or by appointment during unscheduled hours.
venue.seasonal_notes: A notice carried on every page of the site says the gardens and cafe are closed for the season.
venue.price_year_or_season: Single day pass valid September 1, 2026 to May 1, 2027; annual adult membership valid April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027

programs.name: Self-guided garden visit
programs.description: Admission to the 12 acre gardens and trails is by a $10 single day pass or an $80 annual adult membership. Nuu-chah-nulth citizens and children aged 0 to 12 are free. The site says to buy tickets on arrival or to show proof of purchase at check in, and passes can also be bought through the online store. A map of the gardens and the surrounding campus can be downloaded from the gardens page. The site does not describe any guided tour, workshop, group rate or group booking route, and no minimum or maximum group size is published.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the trails through 12 acres of coastal temperate rainforest, stopping at viewpoints that look out over the inlet and at carvings set along the way. The site asks visitors to move slowly, listen to the cedar trees and notice the moss on the branches.
programs.our_note: Children 12 and under get in free, so most of what a group pays is the adults at $10 each. The site says nothing about washrooms, anywhere to eat a packed lunch, or a rate for a group, and a notice on the site says the gardens are closed for the season, so call before you set a date.
programs.practical_summary: The address, opening hours and admission are published, and the whole visit is outdoors on rainforest trails. Washrooms, indoor lunch space, rain backup, bus parking and any group rate are not stated anywhere, so it is worth a call first.
programs.extra_fees_note: Children aged 0 to 12 are free. Anyone 13 or older needs a $10 day pass. The site mentions discounted rates for seniors and youth on memberships but does not publish those prices.
programs.evidence: NUU-CHAH-NULTH CITIZENS & CHILDREN (0-12 YRS) ARE FREE.

conflicts.note: Their site says two different things about opening hours. The gardens page says open seven days a week from 9am to 5pm, and a notice on every page says the gardens and cafe are closed for the season. Worth a phone call before you set a date.

Two of their pages give different numbers for bookings. One says 236-233-2518 and the other says 236-312-6727, which elsewhere is listed as the cafe. We use the first. If it does not get you anywhere, try the other.
